title: Nine Killed Including Five Bangladeshi Nationals in Kolkata Hotel Fire
excerpt: A devastating fire at Shikha Inn on Free School Street leaves nine dead — including a child — as authorities suspect an electrical short circuit and order an inquiry.
body:
• Nine people, including five Bangladeshi nationals and a child, died in a fire at Shikha Inn hotel on Kolkata's Free School Street early Wednesday
  • Approximately 80 people were rescued from the multi-story building, which operates as both a hotel and residential complex
  • Authorities suspect the blaze was caused by an electrical short circuit, possibly from an air conditioning unit
  • West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has ordered an inquiry into the incident

Deadly Blaze on Free School Street

A fire tore through a hotel in central Kolkata early Wednesday morning, killing nine people including five Bangladeshi nationals and a child, officials said, in one of the deadliest building fires in the city in recent years.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2090044336281141389

The blaze broke out at Shikha Inn on Free School Street, a busy commercial strip in the heart of the city popular with budget travelers and business visitors. Firefighters rushed to the scene and rescued approximately 80 people trapped in the multi-story structure, which operates as both a hotel and a residential complex.

Among the dead were five citizens of neighboring Bangladesh, underscoring the building's role as a transit point for cross-border travelers. A child was also among the victims. Several others were hospitalized with injuries, though the exact number of injured remained unclear as rescue operations continued through the morning.

Electrical Fault Suspected

Preliminary investigations suggest the fire may have been caused by an electrical short circuit, possibly originating from an air conditioning unit, a fire department official told Reuters. However, a formal investigation has been ordered and the exact cause has not been officially determined.

"We rescued around 80 people from the building. Many were asleep when the fire broke out and had to be evacuated through windows."

— Kolkata Fire Department official

The fire department deployed multiple engines to contain the blaze, which spread rapidly through the building's corridors. Video footage from the scene showed thick black smoke billowing from upper floors as firefighters worked to bring the fire under control.

Chief Minister Orders Inquiry

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered an inquiry into the fire, as questions mounted about fire safety compliance in commercial buildings across the city. Free School Street, located in the Esplanade area, is lined with older buildings that house hotels, restaurants, and shops — many of which have been flagged by safety inspectors in the past.

Fire safety enforcement in India's densely populated urban centers has long been a contentious issue. Building owners frequently flout safety codes, and enforcement remains inconsistent. High-profile fires in hotels, hospitals, and commercial complexes have periodically jolted authorities into crackdowns, but compliance tends to slip once public attention fades.

Kolkata has seen several deadly building fires in recent years. In 2023, a fire in a multi-story building in the Gariahat area killed several residents, prompting a short-lived push for stricter enforcement. The pattern of tragedy followed by inquiry followed by inaction has become grimly familiar.

Questions for Building Owners

The Shikha Inn fire is likely to intensify scrutiny of fire safety standards in Kolkata's hotel and hospitality sector. Budget hotels and guesthouses in older commercial districts often operate in buildings that lack adequate fire exits, sprinkler systems, and smoke detectors — the basic infrastructure that can mean the difference between life and death in a fire.

The presence of Bangladeshi nationals among the victims adds a diplomatic dimension to the tragedy. Bangladesh's foreign ministry has not yet issued a formal statement, but consular officials are expected to assist with identification of the deceased and repatriation of remains.

As Kolkata mourns, the fire stands as another grim reminder of the human cost of lax safety enforcement in one of India's most storied cities.
nri_angle: The deaths of Bangladeshi nationals in a Kolkata hotel highlight fire safety failures in buildings frequently used by South Asian travelers, and underscores an ongoing concern for diaspora families visiting the region.
